subject.title: Feature: durable natural-language rule learning + explicit multi-mention reply semantics

question: Should OpenClaw define a first-class durable conversational rule-governance layer and cross-channel explicit multi-bot mention semantics, or keep durable learning in memory/plugins while fixing Feishu mention bugs separately?
rationale: The answer determines memory authority, persisted rule/log shape, conflict precedence, possible opt-in policy surface, and whether multi-bot reply semantics are core-wide or channel-owned.

options.title: Keep Broad Design Tracker
options.body: Keep #41366 open for maintainer-sponsored product design and use the open Feishu issues for narrow message-loss fixes.

options.title: Split Durable Rules From Mentions
options.body: Move the durable-rule layer into a separate product proposal and leave this issue to track only explicit multi-mention semantics.

options.title: Route Through Plugin/API Design
options.body: Require proof that existing memory/plugin APIs cannot express durable rule learning before adding a new core rule layer.

recommendation.title: Keep Broad Design Tracker
recommendation.body: Keep #41366 open for maintainer-sponsored product design and use the open Feishu issues for narrow message-loss fixes.

likelyOwner.reason: kasangyong is the clearest current-history signal across the prompt, memory-promotion, and Feishu source paths touched by this design question.
